title: Install the harness and initialize another repository with one command
goal: Let developers initialize this harness in a different repository with one or two short commands, without copying project-specific feature data or overwriting their files.
in_scope: Package the existing dependency-free harness CLI as an installable Python command named `harness`, available from the repository's Git source.

Add a `harness init` command that operates on the current working directory and scaffolds a blank feature registry, feature directory, MVP summary, requirements templates, harness instructions, and the project's three local skills: requirements interview, architecture planning, and feature implementation.

Support one-command initialization through `uvx --from git+https://github.com/jtrimind/hackathon harness init`, and document the reusable install option `uv tool install git+https://github.com/jtrimind/hackathon` followed by `harness init`.

Make initialization safe and repeatable: create missing files, preserve existing project content, avoid duplicate instruction blocks, and report any existing files that need manual review rather than silently overwriting them.
Make globally installed CLI commands operate on the target repository's current working directory while preserving direct `python harness.py` usage in a repository checkout.
Update README.md with prerequisites, install and init commands, generated files, conflict behavior, and next steps.
out_of_scope: Forking or embedding Q00/ouroboros core or requiring its runtime.
Configuring an AI runtime, MCP server, or user-level global skills outside the target project.
Publishing the package to a package index.
acceptance_criteria: The project can be initialized from its Git source with the documented `uvx` command, and the installed CLI supports `harness init`.
Initialization creates a blank project scaffold and copies only generic templates and skills, not this repository's feature registry or project requirements.
Running init twice does not duplicate content or overwrite existing user-authored files.
Existing project files that cannot be merged safely are preserved and reported clearly.
After initialization, feature and requirement commands operate on the target repository rather than the CLI installation directory.
The existing direct script workflow remains available.
